correctness.rationale: For every K and T>0, the explicitly given positive log amplitudes satisfy exact adjacent crossing identities. At each of K crossing times two amplitudes agree and all other m-2 are at most eta^2 of them, giving Fourier ratio >1.99. At the K+1 separating endpoint/midpoint times one amplitude dominates and every other is at most eta times that amplitude, giving ratio <1.43. Analyticity and compact-interval extrema yield K strict interior maxima and K-1 strict minima. For arbitrary B, equalizing q heat-damped cosine amplitudes at fixed t* gives exact ratio sqrt(2q), while the initial ratio tends to sqrt(2), establishing unbounded amplification. A standalone checker reproduces rational crossing identities and numerical unaliased DFT values in 197 tests; finite tests are supplementary.

value.rationale: Recent Fourier-ratio sampling works treat its square as an effective spectral dimension and study whether PDE smoothing reduces that complexity. The explicit construction proves arbitrarily many genuine reversals under a positivity-preserving heat semigroup and unbounded transient expansion of the same natural invariant for real analytic mean-zero data. This is a structural limitation of monotone spectral-preconditioning interpretations, not a routine single-mode numerical check; it identifies assumptions required for any uniform temporal-compressibility statement.
